sm: This LifeNews piece, from Monica Snyder of Secular Pro-Life, challenges a September 2024 NBC News story headlined as a dramatic rise in pregnant women dying in Texas after its abortion ban. NBC relied on an unpublished analysis from the Gender Equity Policy Institute, which said Texas maternal mortality rose 56 percent from 2019 to 2022, versus 11 percent nationwide. The author argues the institute's own numbers show deaths falling after the Heartbeat Law took effect in September 2021, with nearly all the increase coming during COVID in 2020 and 2021. She says Texas had a bigger pandemic spike than the nation. The 2026 Texas report puts the 2021 ratio at 39.1 per 100,000 live births, or 23.5 without COVID, so COVID accounted for roughly 40 percent of Texas maternal deaths that year, versus about 34 percent nationally.

The article cites the newest Texas Maternal Mortality and Morbidity Review Committee report, which found the ratio fell to 20.5 deaths per 100,000 live births by 2024, similar to before 2020. The pregnancy-related ratio fell from 30.0 in 2021 to 20.7 in 2024. Demographer Lyman Stone compared Texas with Northeastern pro-choice states after excluding COVID deaths and found no skyrocketing. A 2026 JAMA Network Open study built a stand-in Texas from states without restrictions and found no statistically significant increase in maternal deaths, including across all 14 states with major post-Dobbs restrictions. The author adds that about three in four Texas pregnancy-related deaths were potentially preventable, citing mental health, hypertensive disorders, gaps in care after birth, and racial disparities. She points to California's quality care collaborative as a model and argues that blaming abortion restrictions diverts attention from real, preventable causes.
